## Data Exploration

The data used in this markdocument are dated 2021-04-21. The tables below
summarise the primary variable of interest **Battery** with four 
categorical covariates to guide experimental design. The battery data will be subset by specific brands for each covariate if the levels across those brands contain enough samples for analysis. 

**Battery - Flash Type**

COXPH - Flash Type, Battery (Procell, Varta)

```{r table - flash type, echo=FALSE} 
tab_ft
```

**Battery - Battery Type**

Can examine lithium vs alkaline ignoring battery brand.

```{r table - battery type, echo=FALSE} 
tab_bt
```

**Battery - Season**

COXPH - Season, Battery (Procell, Varta)

```{r table - season, echo=FALSE}
tab_seas
```

**Battery - Region**

COXPH - Region, Battery (Varta)

```{r table - region, echo=FALSE}
tab_reg
```

\newpage
## Survival Curves

**Semi-parametric (COXPH) vs Non-Parametric (Kaplan-Meier) Survival**

```{r survival curve - coxph vs km bb + fpd + dpd, echo=FALSE}
plot_surv_svn
```

The solid lines show Kaplan-Meier survival estimates. The translucent thick lines show
Cox Proportional-Hazard survival curves. The Cox curves largely follow the Kaplan-Meier survival curves with Maxell being an exception. Varta is the highest performing brand while Procell is the worst.

\newpage
**Semi-parametric (COXPH) vs Parametric (Weibull) Survival**

```{r survival curve - coxph vs weibull bb + fpd + dpd, echo=FALSE}
plot_surv_svp
```

The dashed lines show Weibull survival curves. The translucent thick lines show
Cox Proportional-Hazard survival curves. The Weibull curves follow the Cox PH curves for the three lowest performing battery brands but show reduced survival for the four best performing brands.

\newpage
**Semi-parametric (COXPH) and Daylight Photos per Day (dpd)**

```{r survival curve - coxph bb + dpd, echo=FALSE}
plot_surv_dpd
```

The Cox Proportional-Hazard survival curves are stratified by battery brand (colour) 
and the rate of daylight photos taken. The dotted, dashed and solid lines show five, fifty and ninty-five percent quartiles respectively. Incresing rate of daylight photos shows a small decrese in battery survival. 

\newpage
**Semi-parametric (COXPH) and Flash Photos per Day (fpd)**

```{r survival curve - coxph bb + fpd, echo=FALSE}
plot_surv_fpd
```

The Cox Proportional-Hazard survival curves are stratified by battery brand (colour) 
and the rate of flash photos taken. The dotted, dashed and solid lines show five, fifty and ninty-five percent quartiles respectively. Incresing rate of flash photos shows a moderate decrese in battery survival. 


\newpage
## COXPH Forest Plots

**COXPH Forest - Battery Brand, Flash Photos per Day, Daylight Photos per Day**

```{r forest plot - bb + fpd + dpd, echo=FALSE}
plot_for
```

Battery type has a large significant effect on proportional hazard. There is a small but significant increase in hazard for flash photography. 

\newpage
**COXPH Forest - Battery Type, Flash Photos per Day, Daylight Photos per Day**

```{r forest plot - bt + fpd + dpd, echo=FALSE}
plot_for_bt
```

Unsurprisingly there is a significant and large increase in hazard for 
akaline batteries. Oddly there is a small but significant reduction in 
hazard for flash photos when just considering battery type and flash 
type as covariates.

\newpage
**COXPH Forest - Seasonal data with Procell and Varta brands**

```{r forest plot - bb + seas - varta and procell, echo=FALSE}
plot_for_seas_b
```

There is small but significant reduction in hazard during Autumn.

\newpage
**COXPH Forest - Regional data with Varta brand**

```{r forest plot - reg + fpd + dpd - varta, echo=FALSE}
plot_for_reg
```

Examining regional differences with Varta batteries, there are significant increases in hazard for the central, south east and west regions.
